_readme: STABLE COLD FAILURES — the roster of golden-set cases that are HARD assertions (NOT knownIssue, NOT excused by anything) and that fail on EVERY COLD run of run-eval.ts (`--nocache`, which also sends nosave=1 and debug=1). The set is measured as the exact INTERSECTION over three restarted cold runs on one build, never from a single run's total — that is what makes a documented rotator distinguishable from a new member. This file exists so that 'is this a NEW cold failure?' is a diff instead of a reading exercise: the set previously lived only in prose across three documents, they disagreed about its size, and a ten quietly became a nine with nothing in the repo noticing. Check a cold run against it with: npm run eval:cold-set. Members here are STANDING DEBT, not absolution — every one still reds a cold run, exactly as it should.
_notTheSameAs: known-issue-baseline.json / known-issue-baseline-cold.json are the OPPOSITE population and answer a different question. Those pin the per-case OBSERVED VALUES (foodId, foodName, grams, kcal100, abstained, errored, itemCount) of cases flagged `knownIssue` in golden-set.json — cases that are already EXCUSED, whose failure run-eval deliberately does not count (evalExitCode ignores them), and whose only remaining signal is DRIFT: 'still failing, but failing DIFFERENTLY', reported explicitly NON-GATING at run-eval.ts:427. This file pins MEMBERSHIP, not values, for cases that are NOT excused: they are real red and they fail the suite. The two sets are provably disjoint — no id below appears among the 21 knownIssue ids in golden-set.json, nor among the 20 ids pinned in known-issue-baseline.json (verified 2026-08-19). A knownIssue case can therefore never be a member here, and the checker enforces that.
_naming: The nightly WARM sweep prints a bare count for its own, different set: `known issues still failing: N` (10 of 21 on 2026-08-19, with 11 now passing). This set's size is also nine-or-ten-ish, is measured on a different instrument (COLD, not warm), over a different population (HARD, not excused), and means the opposite thing. Two bare numbers of similar magnitude on one page is exactly how the ten-that-became-a-nine survived. So this set is never 'the failures' and never a bare N: it is `stable cold failures`, and check-stable-cold-failures.ts stamps that label on every line it prints.
_notAnAllowlist: This file is a DETECTOR for the cold session gate, never an excuse list. It is not read by flywheel-sweep.ts, it is not wired to --allow-fail (which defaults EMPTY by design and is pinned by the doc-check claim `flywheel-allow-fail-defaults-empty`), and it cannot turn a red nightly green. The nightly goes green when real failures get FIXED. Membership here is the standing bill; the way a member leaves is check-stable-cold-failures.ts reporting LEFT THE SET after someone fixed it, confirmed over 2-3 cold runs, and then removed it from this file.
_rotatorsNote: All three rotators are AI serving-gram draws (count_unit_ai / AiGeneratedServing). That is the single mechanism this set flaps on, and it is separately unowned. If a NEW rotator is proposed, check whether it is the same mechanism before adding it here rather than fixing it.

confirmedAgainst.note: Three cold runs, same build, minutes apart, recipe-api restarted before each, taken immediately AFTER the #398 deploy (A25/D9b window). Per-run real-failure counts 11/10/10; the INTERSECTION was exactly the nine members below. n-serv-57 LEFT on all three runs and is moved to `departed`. Rotating seats filled every extra slot and nothing else: n-brand-02 (run 1), n-svd-03 (run 1), n-serv-26 (run 2), n-svd-04 (run 3). n-svd-04 is STILL NOT added to `rotators` — the reasoning of the previous entry stands and this is its second flap in ~27 recorded runs, which is not yet evidence of a rotator. Every one of those four also flapped on the UNCHANGED base tree in the same session's local A/B (BASE w5NtCWvzKYwjMNVVVr2CG read 11/11/11 with n-brand-02 and n-serv-26 rotating), so none is attributable to #398. Previous confirmation: T_pVsW6iVzKDqE_E9Y8OE, 2026-08-27, intersection 10.

causeLegend.PANEL: the winning record's own nutrition panel is wrong (usually an uncaught corrupt OFF row, corruptReason NULL)
causeLegend.SERVING: the right record is picked but the wrong serving rung bills it
causeLegend.PICK: retrieval or ranking selects the wrong record
causeLegend.IDENTITY: the record is a brandless stub carrying a different food's values — repairing its panel would still miss the band

members.reason: off_9348470000900 'Unsweetened Almond Milk' carries kcal100=60 against a [10, 45] band (real ~13-17). Its panel is Atwater-coherent but physically impossible (fiber 4.8 g vs fat 3.5 g per 100 ml), so the calories were computed from wrong macros; corruptReason is NULL, so no detector reaches it. Explicitly NOT a modifier-drop case — the query already resolves to a record NAMED 'Unsweetened Almond Milk'.

Bare 'apple' cold-resolves to off_9333022029263 at kcal100=23.9 against a [35, 75] band (real ~52). The panel is Atwater-INcoherent on its own macros, corruptReason is NULL, and the 1-token name puts it squarely in the ~61% detector-unreachable population. Warm is green only because the key was repointed to FDC 171688 as a human-triage pin on 2026-08-03; cold retrieval has never selected that record unaided.

Bare 'mayonnaise' bills fs_34194 at 14.7 g — grams INSIDE the intended band — but the record is a LIGHT-mayo panel (390 kcal/100g) sitting under the bare generic name, so total.calories=57.0 falls under the [60, 180] band. Warm is masked by a human-triage FoodMapping row; the failure is the panel, not the rung.

Bare 'bacon' bills 5 g against a [10, 40] band. That 5 g is FatSecret's own default label on fs_1517, '1 thin slice (yield after cooking)'; in-band 8/12/28 g labels exist on the SAME record and are never picked, because fs_default_serving is deliberately not in the serving guard's REPLACE_TIERS. The PR D pt3 cured/breakfast-meat lexicon default (~28 g) therefore never fires here.

Bare 'pepper jack' bills 2.5 g against an [18, 40] band. The winner off_0858815007307's ONLY serving label is the degenerate '100 g (100 g)' placeholder, which is billed and then CAPPED 100 -> 2.5 g by the spice lexicon matching the contained 'pepper' token: label_serving_default sits in plain CAP_TIERS, while the head-gate fix protects only bare_label_serving. NOTE: the golden-set note's premise of a 'genuine 28 g slice label' is FALSE for this particular winner.

The documented #18 brand-bearing chain regression: 'noodles and company pad thai' bills a brandless retail dry-noodle record (off_4099100064773, 127.5 g via bare_name_sibling_serving) instead of fs_81276 [Noodles & Company]. fs_81276 now carries NULL per-100g calories and a gramless serving, which plausibly handicaps it at admission/scoring. The 2026-07-25 warm recovery was a pure cache eviction, not a retrieval fix, which is exactly why the case is still red cold.

DELIBERATE RED per its golden-set note. PR #235 (2026-08-04) added a total.calories band precisely so the ~30% over-bill would stop being invisible: cold maps '1 cup cooked black beans' to a saucy OFF composite (off_0039400019442) at 240 g / 295 kcal against the USDA reference 172 g / 227 kcal. It was green for months on scale-free kcal100/carbs100 bands that cannot see grams. Expected red until the source-score asymmetry is fixed.

Bare 'tofu' resolves to off_3070451041461 'Tofu' at kcal100=13.3, so protein100=0.9 misses its [5, 22] band. Originally filed as PANEL; ADJUDICATED AND REVERSED 2026-08-13 to IDENTITY — the record is a brandless stub carrying House Foods Tofu Shirataki values, so repairing its panel would still miss the band. Not a rotator: 19 consecutive cold failures spanning seven build ids as of 2026-08-14.

'12 m&ms' bills grams=264 against a [6, 25] band on fs_72448178 "M&M'S" [Cold Stone Creamery] — a mix-in record whose serving rows carry no grams, discarded as no_nutrition until K3 (#390, deployed 2026-08-26) stopped rejecting gram-less FS rows. Cold it now outranks the OFF fun-size row. Conditional on that win the billed grams are a DRAW: 264 on four observed draws, 22 on a fifth (22 g / 110 kcal would PASS the band), tier fs_default_serving — so the 264 is the record's own serving row, not K3's synthetic kcal/2 grams. The resurrection is K3's; the draw is not. COLD-ONLY and unreachable by live traffic: the warm cache row is keyed 'm ms' -> off_00005579 (usedCount 363, untouched) while the cold pipeline keys "m m's", the documented apostrophe/plural fork. The K3 gate could not have seen it — a record that stops returning null is a POOL change, and its 48-seed cross-snapshot arm was venue lines plus controls. The real fix is the resurrected-record pick class (same-name cross-source picks where K3 newly admits a gram-less FS record), A8 pick-family work rather than a per-seed hack; this entry documents the debt and excuses nothing.

rotators.reason: AI serving-gram draw on the AiGeneratedServing path: the SAME record (fs_79482119) returned 40 / 50 / 45 / 60 g across four runs, crossing the band. A second flap mechanism sits upstream — 'one bar' is consumed as quantity+unit so the ONE brand token never reaches retrieval, and exact_match then tie-breaks five identically-scored 'Birthday Cake' records in gather order. Failed 1 of the 3 confirming runs (92 of 158 cold runs on record). Presence is NOT a new member.

count_unit_ai draw variance on a fixed record: the same fs_4578 row every run, with grams drawing 45 / 240 / 30 across three runs. The 25 g floor holds and there is no ceiling, so the high draws blow the band. Failed 1 of the 3 confirming runs (15 of 158 cold runs on record).

'1 glug of olive oil' -> fs_34212 'Olive Oil', tier count_unit_ai, with grams walking 5 -> 10 -> 15 (44.2 / 88.4 / 132.6 kcal) against a [7, 40] band, so run 1 fails and runs 2-3 pass. Classified as pure noise (rotating seat) since its first measurement. Failed 2 of the 3 confirming runs (28 of 158 cold runs on record).

departed.fixedBy: backend #398 (D9b, A25): getCategoryChangePenalty() charges the UNMATCHED SHARE of a candidate's in-set tokens instead of a flat 0.50 on the first unmatched one, so the five real Kirkland protein bars stop paying full price for `cookie` — their own flavour name — while the granola bar pays nothing
departed.confirmedBy: PASSED 3/3 restarted cold runs on sGg_Kx8wKgMGPR53tnEPF, byte-identical: off_0096619505128 "Chocolate chip cookie dough protein bar" [Kirkland], 60 g, 220.2 kcal, kcal100 367, conf 0.95, tier bare_label_serving. Also 3/3 on the pre-deploy local branch build VLD7WD-FUB2Aepro9-YiW against BASE w5NtCWvzKYwjMNVVVr2CG at 11/11/11 with this as the only STABLE-FIXED member and STABLE-INTRODUCED 0. departed.previousReason: 'kirkland protein bar chocolate chip' billed grams=24 against a [40, 80] band on 'Chocolate Chip Chewy Granola Bar' — a granola bar, not the Kirkland protein bar. The roster carried this as a K2 head-noun ADMISSION failure; that account is wrong and A22/A25 measured it. The admitted pool is 9 and CONTAINS the correct record: every Kirkland protein bar is named "... Chocolate chip cookie dough ..." and therefore does spell `chip`, so the every()-gated must-have tokens never delete it. It was decided at RANKING, by 0.008, inside getCategoryChangePenalty(): `chocolate`, `chip` and `bar` are all in CATEGORY_CHANGING_TOKENS and all exempt because the query spells them, so the flat first-hit charge landed on `cookie` for every real protein bar (-0.50) and on nothing for the granola bar, whose only extra in-set token is absent from the set entirely. Owner: mobile:sync-docs/reports/2026-08-28_a25-the-category-penalty-charges-the-right-product.md and 2026-08-28_a25-design-the-charge-becomes-the-unmatched-share.md

departed.reason: THE TEN THAT BECAME A NINE, and the reason this file exists. '1 tsp salt' joined the set on 2026-08-18 by an explicit decision to leave it red, and left on 2026-08-19 when PR #357 re-banded it from [2, 3.5] to [4.5, 7] (merged fc1e520). The old band asserted the density guard's own 0.5 g/ml fallback rather than the food: the record's declared tsp weight is read first (6.0 g cold via fs_label_volume_declared, 5.2 g warm via label_unit_match), and table salt is ~6 g/tsp. Measured on disk: it failed all six cold runs from 2026-08-18T23:20Z to 2026-08-19T00:09Z (builds 6X4EdJlSKyX9V-6MWf4ZU and 4dfpiS1YnzVhEjX7u64lZ) and was absent from all three runs on i1BDbnq_b8pC7Hm3gD_bM. Nothing in the repo recorded either the entry or the exit; two documents still said ten. check-stable-cold-failures.ts would have printed NEW MEMBER on 2026-08-18T23:20Z and LEFT THE SET on 2026-08-19T20:25Z.

The PREVIOUS silent transition, and the precedent: '12 m&ms' left the set around 2026-08-15 and was initially recorded as UNATTRIBUTABLE — 'left the cold-gate stable set and I cannot attribute it'. It was attributed only later, to PR #320 bumping RULES_VERSION 2 -> 3 and invalidating every v2 mapping. A detector that names the exit on the run it happens turns that from an archaeology problem into a line of output.
